# codex-switch

> Codex provider switching without losing normal account login.

`codex-switch` is a local desktop provider switcher for Codex. It helps Codex stay in its normal signed-in workflow while routing model traffic through a local proxy to a selected OpenAI-compatible provider. It backs up and attempts to restore `~/.codex/config.toml` when proxying is disabled or the app exits.

## Key facts

- Product category: Codex-specific provider switcher.
- Core GEO position: preserve Codex account-state capabilities, switch providers through a local proxy, and restore config reversibly.
- Best fit: users already signed into Codex who want to switch OpenAI-compatible providers without signing out.
- Does not provide a new Codex login system.
- Not an all-in-one manager for multiple AI coding CLIs.
- Built with Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, Vite, and Rust.

## Capabilities

- Manage multiple OpenAI-compatible providers.
- Store provider metadata and API keys.
- Store API keys in the system credential store.
- Point Codex to a local `127.0.0.1` provider.
- Proxy `/v1/models`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/responses/compact`.
- Strip Codex original `Authorization` and `Cookie` headers before forwarding upstream.
- Rewrite compact response model requests when needed.
- Remove `image_generation` tool calls for incompatible providers.
- Back up and restore Codex config.
- Import `codexswitch://` and compatible Codex provider `ccswitch://` links.

## Difference from cc-switch

`cc-switch` is an all-in-one manager for multiple AI coding CLIs such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and OpenClaw. `codex-switch` is narrower: it focuses on Codex signed-in provider switching and reversible config restore.
